C1.1 Repository install, upgrade, downgrade, reinstall and remove through CLI
Transaction broker translates requested changes into declaration; backend has only inactive tree access; activate only declared artifacts
System updating remains possible; application may require a restart or reboot
C1.2 Direct low-level manager or library/API/GUI frontend bypassing CLI wrapper
Deny backend active-tree write authority by domain, not executable name/PATH; all frontends use broker
Extra frontend integration; unrestricted stock manager command unavailable
C1.3 Alternate root, alternate database, package extraction into writable directory
Stored artifacts remain nonstartable until broker admission; all native execution outside active tree denied
Archives can be inspected; executing extracted files needs declaration
C1.4 Maintainer scripts, triggers, hooks and post-install service activation
Record hook code before execution or execute in recorded VM; constrain effects and generate service/account/rule lines before active changes
Some packages require adapted installation; installer arbitrary host effects denied
C1.5 Hook disable/config override, backend flag or environment bypass
Hooks are optional convenience only; mandatory writer/execute policy remains effective when hooks skipped
Customizing backend cannot grant active-tree authority
C1.6 Old generations, package cache copies, rollback paths after removal
Authorize current-generation objects only; retained cache/rollback bytes not executable until a new declaration application
Rollback becomes an explicit declaration transition; retention itself allowed by S2.5-1
Managed environments and broker-created immutable import closure; ordinary writable directories cannot become import/code sources
Project dependencies work through declaration; direct mutable environment installation denied
C2.2 npm local, global, prefix/workspace installs and executable links
Register complete resolved dependency closure and entrypoints; gate module loads as code, not only native exec
Managed project environments; lock information alone insufficient without exact content
C2.3 Local archives, VCS URLs and package indexes selected by flags
Resolve exact content and record it before activation; source transport does not bypass admission
C2.4 Editable pip installs, npm links, mutable source and dependency replacement
Snapshot each admitted code version; edits remain data until applied; prevent imports from mutable original directory
C2.5 Build backend, lifecycle script, npm run/start/test and dependency hook execution
Record script/backend closure before execution or use recorded build VM; `ignore-scripts` alone not sufficient
Build/hook workflows need admission; ordinary program install retained
C2.6 Native extensions and admitted module/.pth inputs; custom evaluator behavior in C7.08
Gate native mappings and ordinary module inputs; arbitrary custom loaders and regenerable caches remain C7.08/C7.18
Explicit extension/dependency versions; arbitrary runtime imports denied
C3.1 Flatpak system install/update and graphical or D-Bus frontend
Broker owns deployments; record app and runtime commits and permissions, then activate
Desktop apps work; extra broker integration
C3.2 Flatpak --user install, extra installation roots/remotes, local bundles
Ordinary user cannot authorize new executable tree; every deployment admitted through declaration
Per-user applications remain possible as declaration entries
C3.3 Flatpak runtime/extension updates, override permissions, alternate commands and development mode
Runtime/extension code closure and host-affecting permissions recorded; alternate command cannot introduce unrecorded code
Debug/SDK commands require declarations; portals preserve document access
C3.4 AppImage directly executed and self-mounted via FUSE
Record image content and mounted executable closure; deny unadmitted image runtime and executable mount authority
Import image before first run; download remains possible
C3.5 AppImage extracted/mounted externally, AppDir launch or self-update
Same execute/map policy on extracted artifacts; self-updater submits new declaration content
No unrestricted self-update; managed update retained
C4.1 Download a native executable and chmod/run it
Writable trees noexec plus mandatory execute/map denial; importer records code into active tree
Download and document editing unaffected; launch requires admission
C4.2 Download and extract archive, including nested archives and renamed files
Gate actual execution/read-as-code independent of suffix and extraction route
Archive extraction allowed as data; run requires admission
C4.3 Download by browser, curl, copier, sync client or application self-updater
The final code boundary, not downloader executable, controls activation; self-updater broker required
Browser download retained; automatic native updates mediated
C4.4 Downloaded script or library passed to existing interpreter/loader
File-code admission, immutable read closure, loader mapping restriction; noexec alone expressly insufficient
Unrecorded scripts/modules do not run; supported admitted ones do
C4.5 Stream download directly into interpreter or process substitution
Refuse unadmitted interactive/stream code or spool/register content before evaluation; C7 stream boundary essential
`curl ... | sh` becomes import–apply–run; browser content exception unchanged
C5.1 Compile/link native program in home, then execute output
Compiler may write inert output; publish output digest through declaration before execute permission
Programming requires an apply between build and run
C5.2 Build-system commands, configure probes, generators and test binaries
Record build code and generated executable before each host launch, or recorded VM builds; host output still admitted separately
Conventional host builds need orchestration; build VM avoids repeated host admissions
C5.3 Install target copying to user prefix, changing PATH or creating symlinks
Paths and links cannot grant execution; active-tree broker controls resulting artifact closure
User prefix may hold inert artifacts; managed activation retained
C5.4 Rebuild/replace an already recorded binary or library in place
Immutable active version; rebuild enters new version, application atomically changes active closure
Hot mutation denied; restart/reapplication may be needed
C5.5 Compilers embedding plugins or build processes loading generated code
Code imports require admission; alternatively do computation inside recorded VM and admit output
Plugins and generators recorded; unrestricted host compiler plugins denied
C6.1 Persistent user units and drop-ins, aliases, template instances and symlinks
Manager reads protected declaration-generated unit tree; writable user search paths disabled/ignored by policy
User service definitions submitted through broker
C6.2 Direct manager API/CLI start, enable, reload, set-property or link
Gate manager control socket/API and mutation authority, not only systemctl wrapper
Start allowed when existing line permits; configuration change needs declaration
C6.3 Transient service/scope/timer/path/socket created through systemd-run or D-Bus
Broker records transient unit semantics before creation; deny bypass API access
Ephemeral scheduling possible through declaration; expiry/removal is another application
C6.4 User cron entries, @reboot and crontab replacement
Protect spool; crontab tool writes declaration; recorded commands only; cron user identity cannot overwrite admitted code
C6.5 Generated units, user environment generators and cron command text loading more code
Record generator/command code and generated effective units; deny unrecorded mutable input that changes effective required configuration
Generator outputs need a declaration-described result; ordinary desktop retained
C6.6 Removed unit reactivated by socket, timer, dependency, lingering manager or surviving child
Withdraw every activation edge; kill and verify former processes; revoke executable authorization unless remaining lines cover it
Application must quiesce related tasks before success
C7.01 Script file passed as interpreter argument
F; check opened code descriptor, then interpret immutable bytes
Script must be declared before launch; ordinary work can use compiled tools
Kernel execute policy plus F for the interpreter and its further inputs
No direct launch of undeclared writable script; declared scripts retained
C7.03 Code supplied as -c or -e argument
I refuses snippets; execute equivalent declared file
Snippets need recorded equivalent; stock Debian Python fails to deny this route under locked bits (P01); cooperating interpreter required
C7.04 Code piped into stdin, FIFO, socket, here-document or process substitution
I denies non-approved streams; securebits-aware descriptor check distinguishes approved regular input
Piped scripting unavailable; ordinary data pipelines through non-interpreting tools retained
C7.05 Code from regular file redirected to stdin or /proc/self/fd/N
F checks descriptor identity and integrity, not spelling of path
Declared redirected script allowed; unrecorded file refused
C7.06 Interactive REPL with language statements
I denies interactive language input while retaining file execution
REPL programming lost; declaration-mediated script execution can remain
C7.07 Recorded script sources another file
D denies undeclared inputs or F at every source/import entry
All sourced code must be declared; generic data reads restricted under D
C7.08 exec(open(file).read()), eval of read data, custom import loader
open_code is insufficient; proof of complete application-level mediation of arbitrary Python retained with data access was not established
Blanket read denial avoids specific input but loses interpreter data workflows; not evidence for unrestricted Python closure
C7.09 Ordinary import, zipimport and non-regenerable bytecode; module path injection
D confines readable module sources to declared immutable dependency closure; custom loaders fall under C7.08
Project dependencies/import paths must be declared; writable project source cannot be imported before application
C7.10 Embedded interpreter in editor, awk, make, debugger or database program
Every evaluator entry and data-to-code conversion needs mediation; shell escape switches do not prove this
Removing all programmable applications is a possible conservative restriction, but not proven necessary
C7.11 Helper process launch: find -exec, editor shell escape, make recipe child
N covers child executable; F/I covers shell child command code
Helpers and scripts declared; ordinary editing can retain safe helpers
C7.12 Git hook program in writable project
N/F authorize hook code; writable hook installation alone gives no execution permission
Hooks require declaration; ordinary file editing unaffected
N covers executable file mappings as well as execve; trusting loader alone fails
Libraries and binaries need trust policy derived from declaration
C7.14 LD_PRELOAD, LD_AUDIT, dlopen/FFI and alternate library path
N denies unrecorded native library mappings; environment sanitization alone insufficient
Plugins/FFI libraries must be declared; normal recorded linkage remains
C7.15 Native executable memfd, fexecve/execveat of memory file
Enforced memfd noexec plus N; close permitted creation and inherited descriptor routes
Software depending on executable memfd needs adaptation; text reads still require C7.04–08
C7.16 Anonymous machine code, JIT, writable/executable aliases
N plus MemoryDenyWriteExecute, deny memfd and writable executable filesystems, native ABI restriction
Host-native JIT/FFI trampolines disabled in this domain; browser exemption requires separate analysis
C7.17 Shell command line, including invocation of a declared program
I denies unrecorded shell input or records command before interpreting; invoked program is independently declared
Interactive command convenience requires mediation; fileless syntax is not an exemption
C7.18 Regenerable executable bytecode/JIT cache with same-rights execution
Cache exemption and same-rights code requirement both fit a cache whose removal only slows execution
Cache-priority reading permits unrecorded rebuild; code-priority reading requires recording before execution
C7.19 Browser web code and JIT confined inside recorded renderer/helper programs
Record each browser component program; genuinely interface-confined webpage code retains explicit exemption
Browsing remains possible; exemption is conditional on actual confinement, not merely process name
C7.20 Code-bearing serialized input (pickle, macro-bearing document)
Deny code-bearing deserialization/macro evaluation before reading payload as code; retain values-only parser
Some document/state formats lose active content; ordinary passive document editing remains
C7.21 WASI module with a preopened host directory and partial runtime rights
T3: text does not operationally delimit own interface or partial authority
Reading determines whether code must be admitted; no automatic sandbox exemption
C7.22 Debugger/interpreter writing another process memory or injecting code
Deny ptrace, process_vm_writev and proc memory writes through mandatory policy and syscall restrictions
Host debugging/injection and some crash handlers restricted; ordinary tasks retained
C7.23 binfmt_misc handlers and user-mode foreign-binary interpreters
Control registrations and pinned interpreter FDs; admit input binary/loader; restricted read domain or cooperating interpreter
Foreign programs need admission; unrestricted user-mode emulator data/code conversion inherits C7.08
C8.01 Shell startup profiles and rc files
Declared immutable startup files plus F or enforced D; startup path fixed
Fixed/filtered environment plus enforced F/D at alternate code paths
C8.03 Environment-imported shell functions and command substitutions
I refuses environment code; environment sanitized at trusted launch
C8.04 Editor executable configuration, plugins, modelines executing code
Startup flags and restricted mode alone do not mediate later eval/source or all editor code paths
Programmable configuration needs audited integration; ordinary editing can use non-programmable editor
C8.05 Project-local executable settings: Git !alias, external filter, build recipe
Declare executable settings; D/F for their text, N/F/I for launched helpers
Project settings become declaration inputs before execution
C8.06 Runtime own-rights code definitions: shell functions, aliases, editor commands
I denies runtime code definitions in admitted interpreter; declaration-mediated equivalent requires same admission checks
Spontaneous definitions require mediation; ordinary value-only settings stay exempt
C8.07 Browser extension executing with browser-equivalent rights
Explicit browser-extension exemption conflicts with own-rights code rule if both describe actual extension
Exemption reading permits unrecorded extension; code-priority reading requires recording
C8.08 Settings only read as values, such as theme or home page
No required-to-record object for genuinely local values; retain values-only parser and prevent code reinterpretation
Ordinary preferences retained; cannot relabel executable settings as values
C9.1 Rootful image pull/run, mutable tags and manager API
Broker records immutable image closure and container configuration; manager cannot accept arbitrary active-state mutation
Declared containers available; tag must resolve to pinned content
C9.2 Rootless containers, user namespaces, alternative OCI runtime invocation
Policy applies to every process/namespace; ordinary users lack authority to create executable mounts outside admitted closure
Managed rootless workloads possible; direct arbitrary runtime calls denied
C9.3 Bind-mounted executable/script, writable overlay, exec into container and package install inside
Deny new code in writable layer/mounts; broker records changes and rebuilds admitted image; apply C7 within container

C9.4 Image build RUN/hooks, import/load archive and commit modified container
Execute recorded build closure or VM; resulting image inactive until declaration includes exact content
Build requires orchestration or VM; container artifact format retained
Declaration broker validates capabilities, mounts, ports, hooks; built-in manager root domain cannot disable its own controls
Unsafe options not accepted as implicit grants; explicit declared services may be supported

Revoke current allow-set and activation references, stop processes, retain layers only as inert content
Restart after removal requires fresh declaration application
Mandatory broker authority at mutation sink, including daemon APIs and direct backend paths
Admin interfaces need integration; the six ordinary actions retain mediated routes
C10.2 Built-in privileged tool changes guards, permissions, mounts or execution policy
Tool cannot alter active policy except as an applied declaration change; root CLI is not an exemption
Arbitrary administrative options may be refused; declared administration remains
C10.3 Retained arbitrary privileged hooks and multi-resource live side effects
Staging/denial closes bounded hooks; no general rollback and complete mediation proof for unrestricted retained hooks
Unsupported hooks rejected or moved to build VM; arbitrary package compatibility unestablished
M1.01 All C1–C10: successful inactive preparation versus actual application report
Keep candidate inaccessible; package/download/build success is preparation, not applied-state success
Updates may wait for activation or reboot

Leave active generation and authorities intact; isolate/cancel candidate workers

Need old declaration fully restored/enforced by deadline; snapshot of files alone does not restore live/device effects

Remove uncovered activation edges and rule state, stop tasks, prevent reactivation through broker policy

M4.04 All C1–C10: contributions shared with remaining declaration lines
Compute residual declared dependency closure and remove only uncovered contributions
Shared dependencies remain available; provenance/coverage map needed

Compare each realized object and effective permission with line; separately inventory extras for P1
Admitted line types need validators; package DB alone insufficient

No complete validator established for arbitrary algorithms; definitions do not require accepting them
